## Body

Three lessons from the last four PRs (#200, #204, #210), all merged.

1. A check at read time is not a guard (F149 round 2, spoonbill F001). Registration decided on a roster snapshot under its own lock, but `pij close` doesn't take that lock, and the seat upsert wrote the tombstone fields unconditionally. A close landing between the read and the write was erased. The fix that covers every path goes into the write itself: `upsert_seat` gets `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... WHERE <keeps owner-close>`. When 0 rows are affected it returns `E-RS-SEAT-RETIRED`, and the dropped transaction takes its spine event with it. The deliberate lifts (revive's launch row, a spawn placement, a verified `adopt --reclaim`) use an explicit `Registry::put_lifting_owner_close`; the trait default delegates, so the fakes stay unguarded. Test it with a wrapper `Registry` that commits the close inside `put_reporting` before delegating, against the real SQLite store (reaper_tests' `BindsBeforeCommit` is the pattern). A lock would also have to travel with the owned write across cancellation, so prefer the conditional write.
   Also: a second close of a seat retired for another reason must upgrade the tombstone (F002); a repeat close of an owner-closed seat stays idempotent.

2. Any notice that lists items needs grouping and a byte cap (F150). The prime got an 11 KB idle notice repeating one line dozens of times. Group per (role, instance, project) with a count and the oldest's age, cap the listed text (`HELD_TEXT_MAX` 1,500 bytes) with "...and N more", and test with 40 items. The time-limit alerts still don't group: F161 (kestrel, delivery/**).

3. Giving a pij-rs verb its own help ripples (F156, three CI rounds). `#[command(disable_help_flag = true)]` makes the verb "own its help", and `the_shim_forwards_exactly_the_verbs_that_own_their_help` then requires it in `harness/scripts/pij-native-verbs.json` (biome wraps the list once it's long) and in `.omp/extensions/pij/core/generation-routing.ts` (the type union, the native list, its test). TS tests that used the verb as their example of an HTTP-routed verb break (cli.integration, generation-cutover's "unlisted leaf" and its canonical POST contract cases): swap in `stream`, and filter the shim contract cases to non-native routes. None of this runs locally without node_modules (C25), so read the CI log with `gh run view <id> --log-failed | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -E "FAIL |AssertionError|Formatter"` and fix every failure in one push.

Process (C34): two rounds per PR; mutants are optional, so stop a running set once enough are killed, restore by hand, and check the source-diff hash. After 90 minutes without a PR, send pm-001 one line. A new task gets a new branch and worktree named coder/f<N>-<slug>. Work that lands in another role's owned path (delivery/**) is split to that role, not absorbed.
